target.title: fix: correct Poe provider logo and brand color
target.body:
## Problem

Poe used a malformed provider symbol and the old green brand color. The mismatch was visible on the website and propagated to the app/widget color metadata.

## Changes

- Replace the app and website SVGs with the normalized Poe symbol.
- Use Poe purple `#5D5CDE` in the app descriptor, widget, and website provider card.
- Add a focused regression test locking the Poe icon resource and exact RGB values.
- Add the user-facing changelog entry and thank @garethpaul.

The color and small-size symbol usage were checked against [Poe's official brand guidelines](https://poe.com/pages/brand-guidelines) and the downloadable official logo assets.

## Verification

- `swift test --filter PoeProviderDescriptorTests` — 1 test passed on final head.
- `./Scripts/test_repository_size.sh` — passed on final head.
- `make check` — passed: repository guards, 145 local links, 21 site locales / 139 messages, SwiftFormat clean, SwiftLint 0 violations across 1,246 files.
- `make test` — all 46 shards passed on the Poe implementation before merging the repository-size guard from current `main`; the merge did not touch Poe or runtime code.
- `./Scripts/package_app.sh` — production app bundle built and signed locally.
- Isolated built-app QA — disposable `HOME`, config directories, and Keychain access disabled; Settings filtered to Poe, opened the Poe pane, and rendered the corrected symbol without clipping or credential prompts.
- Local website QA — dark-theme provider grid rendered the corrected Poe mark; `logos/poe.svg` loaded successfully with no page errors.
- Autoreview — clean, no accepted/actionable findings (0.84 confidence).

## Risk

Low. The behavioral surface is limited to Poe branding constants/assets plus a descriptor regression test. Disabled app rows intentionally retain the system monochrome tint; provider purple is used by branded app/widget/site presentation.
